title: Harden scripts/deploy.sh — no guards on a public site
notes: Builds and deploys unconditionally: no dirty-tree refusal, no version read, no rollback target printed, no test gate (there is no suite to gate on). The scraper's equivalent refuses a dirty tree because an image built from uncommitted code cannot be rebuilt from git for a rollback. Same risk here and a public site at the other end. Minimum: refuse a dirty tree, print the currently-serving revision before switching, print the rollback command after.

title: HEAD returns 405 on every public page — including /
notes: Every route is @app.get/@app.post; FastAPI does not synthesise HEAD for a GET route, so HEAD / -> 405 while GET / -> 200 (confirmed live, not inferred). Real clients hit it: ShapBot across /, /privacy, /terms, /imprint, /auth/google on 08-27, and a Chrome/96 agent on HEAD / on a regular cadence that reads as an uptime monitor. Nobody is locked out — the cost is that the site looks down to link checkers, unfurl bots and monitors, and any future uptime alerting on HEAD would be wrong from day one. Invisible to the audit's own check because curl defaults to GET. Not the wp2shell POST 405s, which are hostile scans correctly rejected. Developer must name the mechanism chosen (@app.head per route vs api_route methods=[GET,HEAD]) and why. Spec: W-005-head-requests-405.md

title: Race.mv_id mapped as Text but the column is uuid — an armed 500
source: exports/reports/20260808_new_tickets_from_bugs.md Ticket F (gitignored — evidence quoted in the spec)
notes: core.v_denormalized_event_data_upcoming.mv_id is uuid; app/models/core.py:17 declares mapped_column(Text, primary_key=True). Ordinary reads never filter on mv_id so nothing is broken today. The mismatch bites when SQLAlchemy issues WHERE mv_id = :pk, which happens whenever a Race is expired and re-accessed: Postgres rejects it with 'operator does not exist: uuid = character varying'. Already hit once in production development — an early _heal_defaulted_terrain committed on the request session, expiring the in-flight Race rows, and the next attribute access 500'd the whole event page. It shipped with a workaround (commit on a separate Session) and event_image_service.py:175 now carries a comment explaining the landmine rather than defusing it. Any future code that commits the request session mid-render, or calls refresh()/expire_all() on a Race, re-arms the same 500. grep shows mv_id read nowhere but the declaration, so the blast radius is the mapping itself. p2 not p3: the failure mode is a 500 on a page render triggered by an unrelated change, and the diagnosis cost is high against a one-line fix. Spec: W-007-mv-id-uuid-mapping.md

title: dev.sh's service lifecycle: readiness unchecked, a held port, and teardown that timeout does not reach
source: docs/DEV_NOTES.md 2026-08-28 (while on W-001); second mode DEV_NOTES 2026-08-28 (while on W-005), folded in at the W-005 review
notes: TWO FAILURE MODES OF THE SAME FUNCTION OF THE SAME SCRIPT; the second was added 2026-08-28 from the W-005 review, where the developer's DEV_NOTES entry asked the PM to decide between folding it here or cutting a new ticket. FOLDED HERE, because both are scripts/dev.sh deciding a service is ready when it has not checked. (1) THE SLEEP: suspected, read from source not reproduced. dev.sh starts the Cloud SQL proxy in the background then 'sleep 1' with the comment 'Give it a moment to bind'. If the proxy is slower than a second, uvicorn starts against nothing listening on 5432 and the failure surfaces as a DB error, sending the reader after the wrong problem. The developer's note walks back the more alarming framing it opens with: the leak-on-lost-race path is already guarded, because kill -0 covers a PROXY_PID that never bound. What survives is only the fixed sleep. Fix is a bounded poll on the port replacing the sleep, failing loudly with a named reason on timeout rather than handing uvicorn a dead socket. (2) THE HELD PORT — VERIFIED, HIT ON W-005, AND THE MORE DANGEROUS OF THE TWO: dev.sh skips starting the proxy if something already holds 5432, and uvicorn --port 8000 simply loses the bind if something already holds 8000, yet dev.sh prints its usual startup lines either way. On this machine a uvicorn from the MAIN CHECKOUT had been up since Aug 23 on 8000; dev.sh run from the W-005 worktree exited clean and every probe went to a server running MASTER, NOT THE BRANCH. The first sweep returned 405 on every page - the exact defect being fixed. Caught only because 405 vs 200 is maximally loud. THE INVERSE IS THE REAL RISK: a subtler ticket (template tweak, filter boundary, copy change) returns PLAUSIBLE output from the wrong checkout, and 'verified in the browser' gets written in good faith about code that never ran. With no test suite (W-003) that sentence is the ONLY evidence a review has, so this failure mode FORGES THE ARTEFACT THE REVIEW DEPENDS ON - which is why this is no longer purely local-tooling hygiene. Detection that worked: 'ss -ltnp | grep :8000' then 'ls -l /proc/<pid>/cwd', the decisive one, which names the checkout being served. Developer must NAME the choice for a held port - refuse, pick a free one, or print the serving checkout's path - and the same question applies to 5432. Three terminals share this checkout, so killing the holder is NOT the default. Out of scope: any change to the worktree workflow itself; adding a test suite (W-003). AMENDED 2026-10-26, THIRD MODE FOLDED IN from DEV_NOTES (while on W-045): 'timeout 60 bash scripts/dev.sh' did not stop at 60 s. bash defers its EXIT/TERM trap until the foreground uvicorn exits, and timeout's TERM reached bash only, so the proxy and the server outlived it. Ctrl-C works (it signals the process group). Folded rather than dropped because it FEEDS MODE (2): an agent verifying with timeout leaves a uvicorn holding 8000 and a proxy holding 5432, and the next dev.sh run, from any checkout, serves the leftover code. Title widened to cover teardown. Acceptance gains: under 'timeout N bash scripts/dev.sh' both children are gone after N seconds (check with ss -ltnp).

title: Finished events vanish the day after their last race
notes: Spec: tickets/W-012-retain-finished-events.md. PAULO'S IDEA, AND THE ONE THING THAT CHANGES THE ARC — see PLAN.md. The defect is GRAIN, not window length: list_races filters per RACE (race_service.py:157, WHERE at :173-189, race_date >= yesterday) before grouping into events, so an event's visibility is decided by individual races. Two consequences: a finished event drops off ~a day after its last race, and a PARTLY-past multi-day event is already served with its early races silently missing from distances/formats/cutoffs, because the grouping loop only ever sees rows that survived the WHERE. race_date_end (:246-250) is computed after the filter, so it is both the value the fix needs and a value the current filter corrupts. THE DATES ARE THE SPEC, NOT THE PHRASE 'three days': last race Aug 1 -> visible Aug 1-3, absent Aug 4, i.e. today <= last_race_date + 2. Paulo's own example and 'three days' disagree by one; the dates win. STEP 1 CAN STOP THE TICKET: one query decides whether core.v_denormalized_event_data_upcoming still carries past-dated rows (its name says upcoming). If it does not, no filter change here can retain anything - route to the scraper's IDEAS.md with evidence quoted inline and set this blocked. Do NOT widen the filter against a view that cannot supply the data. Naive fix (race_date >= today - 3) passes single-day events and FAILS multi-day and the all-rows-retained requirement. Developer must also decide where a finished event sorts (sort_key puts it at the TOP of an ascending list) and name the choice. p2 not p1: nothing is broken and no data is wrong - the site under-shows, and Paulo flagged it high priority. Out of scope: any visual treatment for a finished event, the TBC arm, the event detail page, core.* changes. AMENDED 2026-10-21 (AUDIT_20261021T0828 F1): STEP 1 HAS BEEN RUN AND STOPS THE TICKET. The gate as written passed on the wrong rows - all 373 past-dated rows in the view are tbc, kept by the view's tbc arm; zero rows from yesterday; the MV holds 406 past non-tbc rows / 103 events the view drops at midnight after D. So D+1/D+2 cannot be built here. Corrected gate and the measurement are in the spec; do not re-run. Waiting on a scraper-side view change, requested in that repo's docs/IDEAS.md 2026-10-21 (scraper afe88c2, web-audit entry: rollover stalled + D+2 view ask). W-016 no longer sequences after this. RE-PRIORITISED 2026-10-22 p2 -> p4: blocked on the scraper view change, and the brief ranks blocked work 4th. Back to p2 when the scraper ships D+2 rows. RE-CONFIRMED 2026-10-24 (AUDIT_20261023T1719 F5): not re-gated, still blocked. Scraper T-134 (the D+2 view/MV change) is open p3 and waits on T-117; T-133 (rollover) is done in scraper 0.79.0. W-040 handles the URL that dies when an edition leaves.

title: core.py's other 53 column declarations have never been checked against the view
source: W-007 review 2026-08-28; the developer's own named follow-up in the 1.9.6 changelog
notes: Spec: tickets/W-014-audit-core-model-column-types.md. HANDED OVER BY W-007, WHICH CORRECTLY SCOPED IT OUT. app/models/core.py declares 54 columns against a view this repo does not own; W-007 checked exactly ONE (mv_id), found it wrong, and left 53 unlooked-at. One sample, one hit. W-007 RAISED THE VALUE OF THIS AUDIT past what it was worth before: the mv_id mapping was wrong in TWO directions and only one was the reported bug - the SQL half (WHERE mv_id = $1::VARCHAR against uuid, which 500'd the page) and the PYTHON half (under Text, SQLAlchemy applied no result processing, so psycopg returned a uuid.UUID OBJECT while the annotation said Mapped[str]). The second was invisible for 18 days and was found only because somebody printed the value while fixing the first. A mismatch that never emits bad SQL can still hand the app a type it did not declare, surfacing as an AttributeError or a malformed template value far from the declaration. Text is declared on 27 of 54 columns, which is where a wrong guess hides best. One information_schema query does the whole audit, one session per the connection budget. THE FINDING MAY BE 'NOTHING' AND THAT IS A REAL RESULT: it converts 'never checked' into 'checked on <date>', which is the actual defect. p3: no user sees it and nothing is known broken, but the one known instance cost a full debugging pass against a one-line fix. Out of scope: any core.* database change (routes to the scraper), app/models/web.py, re-opening the as_uuid=False decision, automating the check (that is W-003). title: BACKLOG.csv is CRLF, so a one-cell edit reads as a whole-board rewrite
source: docs/DEV_NOTES.md 2026-08-28 (while on W-007) — the note asks the PM to decide
notes: Spec: tickets/W-015-backlog-csv-crlf.md. THE NOTE ASKED, THIS IS THE ANSWER: ticketed. The board is the ONE FILE TWO ROLES WRITE TO, and its line endings make an innocent edit indistinguishable from a boundary violation. CRLF while every other tracked text file is LF; a Python read-modify-write silently normalises, so the developer's two-field edit came back as a 14-LINE DIFF - the whole board rewritten, which is exactly the shape docs/roles/README.md says means 'someone crossed the line'. NOT COSMETIC: the single-writer rule is enforced by READING THE DIFF, and an artefact that turns every edit into a full-file diff destroys the signal that rule depends on. The reviewer either loses time proving it was innocent or stops looking, which is worse. Caught only because the diffstat said 28 lines for a two-field change. git diff --check also reports trailing whitespace on every line - that is the CR, not real whitespace. p4 not p5: unlike W-004 and W-009 this degrades a CONTROL and recurs on every edit by either role until fixed. Acceptance requires the conversion commit contain NOTHING ELSE (a content change hidden in a 14-line whole-file diff is the exact failure this prevents) and a .gitattributes guard so the next writer's editor cannot silently undo it. Out of scope: any content change to the board, other files' line endings, changing the CSV format, the single-writer rule itself.

title: Tile price is one race read as a floor, not the event’s range
notes: Spec: tickets/W-016-tile-price-range.md. PAULO'S ASK, PREMISE CORRECTED IN TRIAGE: he wants the tile to show a range across the event's races ('20 - 80EUR'), and that is the whole scope. He believed the tile shows the CHEAPEST race; it does not. list_races takes registration_price and price_currency in the FIRST-SEE branch (race_service.py:242-243), so the tile shows whichever race sorted EARLIEST BY DATE, and race_tile.html:4 renders it with a trailing '+' that asserts a floor. On an event whose earliest race is the ultra, THE TILE PRESENTS THE DEAREST PRICE AS A MINIMUM - wrong data rendered anonymously, which is band 2, hence p2 not p4. The premise correction changed WHY the tile is wrong, not WHETHER. Same bug class ARCHITECTURE.md already records TWICE under the read model (race-level field read off rows[0]: hero terrain, format filter); distances, formats and cutoffs are already collected per-row with comments explaining exactly this, price is the one left behind, so the fix shape is proven ten lines away. TWO CALLS TAKEN IN THE TICKET, not left to the developer: (1) free races render 'Free - EUR123', keeping the template's existing vocabulary rather than a second rendering of zero - Paulo delegated this one; (2) mixed currency within an event renders a single value WITHOUT the '+', never a converted range, and the developer measures the frequency with one query and reports it in the close-out. THE TRAP: 0 and NULL are different and must stay different - the template already branches them (0 -> Free, NULL -> em dash). NULL is UNKNOWN, not free, so an unpriced row is excluded from the range and NEVER becomes the floor. Acceptance enumerates all degenerate cases as tile renders, both tiers. SEQUENCE AFTER W-012: same grouping loop, and W-012's diff moves the lines this one edits. Out of scope: the event detail page's price display, currency conversion, a price filter, the {currency} {price} format itself, core.* (the source values are correct). AMENDED 2026-10-21: the SEQUENCE AFTER W-012 constraint is lifted - W-012 is stopped at Step 1 waiting on the scraper. Do this first; W-012 rebases onto it if the view ever changes.

title: Canonical redirect is still 302 six weeks after the rollout gate expired
notes: Spec: tickets/W-017-promote-canonical-redirect-301.md. FOUND IN A SWEEP OF exports/ideas/, WHICH IS GITIGNORED AND WAS NEVER TRIAGED - evidence quoted inline in the spec because a path under exports/ is unreadable from a worktree. CanonicalDomainMiddleware (app/main.py:63-70) 302-redirects beta. and www. to the apex. 302 WAS CORRECT WHEN IT SHIPPED and is a deliberate temporary state: 301 is cache-poison for rollback, so the escape hatch was kept open on purpose. THE DEFECT IS THAT IT WAS NEVER CLOSED. The gate was '~7 days of no apex regression'; apex shipped 2026-07-27 and it is now 2026-09-08 - six weeks. The gate did not fail, it EXPIRED UNNOTICED because nothing tracked it. Two docs now state the pending action as settled fact (ARCHITECTURE.md:510 and CHANGELOG.md:1013 both say 'promote to 301 once stable'), so a future reader inherits 'this is how it is' rather than 'this is step one of two' - acceptance corrects ARCHITECTURE rather than appending. THE SOURCE FILE'S 'SKIP IF' CLAUSE IS TAKEN, NOT FORWARDED: do NOT skip. It weighed rollback risk against SPECULATIVE SEO value and both sides moved - rollback risk is gone after six weeks, and W-006 (robots.txt) and W-010 (sitemap.xml) now ship canonical-host declarations to crawlers, W-010's acceptance already requiring absolute https://indierunners.co URLs. A sitemap asserting apex is canonical while legacy hosts answer with a TEMPORARY redirect tells a crawler two things. SEQUENCE BEFORE W-006: W-005 set the precedent that the first routing ticket to land decides what the rest inherit. Out of scope: removing beta anywhere (W-018), CDN/DNS-layer redirect (dropped in triage), robots/sitemap themselves, _REDIRECTED_HOSTS/_CANONICAL_HOST.

title: Decommission the beta host — OAuth URI, domain mapping, DNS
notes: Spec: tickets/W-018-decommission-beta-host.md. Items 2-4 of the same untriaged exports/ideas/ rollout note, evidence quoted inline. OPERATOR WORK, NOT A DEVELOPER BRANCH: all three steps are Google Cloud Console and DNS registrar actions, there is no diff, and THE BRANCH COLUMN WILL STAY EMPTY ON PURPOSE - stated so an empty branch on a done row does not later read as a lost record. Paulo executes; the close-out is written into the ticket. One ticket not three because the steps are strictly sequential and share one gate: beta traffic reaching zero. Remove beta from the OAuth Client's Authorized Redirect URIs, then delete the Cloud Run domain mapping, then drop the CNAME - DNS LAST, because that is the step that releases the hostname and dropping it first opens the dangling-CNAME window this ticket closes. THE TRAP, PRESERVED VERBATIM IN THE SPEC: removing the OAuth URI while any traffic remains breaks sign-in, and CanonicalDomainMiddleware CANNOT protect that path - Google only redirects to registered URIs, so a redirected callback loses the code param and the user lands on the apex homepage SIGNED OUT, which reads as 'sign-in is broken' (band 1) rather than failing loudly. Each step is therefore gated on a log check whose output must be QUOTED in the close-out, not asserted, and the sign-in check belongs immediately after step 1 rather than at the end. DEPENDS ON W-017: do not dismantle the escape hatch in the same breath as committing to a cached 301. p4: real takeover shape (dangling CNAME + registered callback) but it needs an attacker to first acquire a hostname that is not currently released. Out of scope: www. (a live alias, staying), the 302->301 promotion, any code change, item 6's informal callback-host monitoring (dropped - see the IDEAS note of 2026-09-08). AMENDED 2026-10-26 (infra I-006 applied): step 2 is now deleting google_cloud_run_domain_mapping.beta in indie-runners-infra/web/domains.tf, plan, apply on Paulo's word. A Console delete would read as drift there. NEXT TICKET (Paulo, 2026-11-09): moved p4 to p2, ahead of W-109.

title: A profile links to event pages the app will not serve
notes: Spec: tickets/W-019-profile-links-404.md.
